hypotheses.explanation: Meshes bypass their named markers because emit uses obj.parent=parent. Consequently, hiding StudyPanel does not reach StudyPanel.001. Desk meshes still follow StudyDesk, but bypass the named Top and Support markers, violating the named part dependency contract.

camera_calibration.reason: set_view directly assigns the requested sensor width, 40.8; only numerical tolerance is expected.

geometry_replay.reason: The emitter explicitly multiplies geometry_frame by the primitive matrix and preserves that world matrix when parenting. No basis-length fault is evident.

position_replay.reason: Primitive origins receive the geometry frame; desk meshes remain descendants of StudyDesk and should receive its final move.

visibility_isolation.reason: The mesh is outside StudyPanel's descendants. If associated emitted meshes are tracked, toggling the marker leaves the mesh unchanged, giving 1; descendant-only discovery finds no meshes and returns 2.

support_relation.reason: StudyDesk still contains all five furniture meshes. support_on computes their world AABB bottom and translates the group to the floor top.

dependency_move.reason: All five desk meshes bypass their named part markers. The contrary-parent fraction should approach 1 even though the meshes follow the furniture move.

material_dependency.reason: Mesh data and materials are copied before editing. The supplied Top.001 edit audit also reports no non-target changes; the expected integer count is zero.

hypotheses.explanation: An alternative repair interpretation treats the sibling marker/mesh arrangement as intentional and attributes the failure to visibility resolving only descendants rather than all meshes associated with a public ID. This is less consistent with the named part dependency requirement, but explains the same visible panel.

camera_calibration.reason: The same direct sensor assignment applies; this probe does not distinguish the hypotheses.

geometry_replay.reason: The visibility interpretation does not change the explicit geometry-frame multiplication.

position_replay.reason: The observed desk hierarchy still carries furniture translation correctly.

visibility_isolation.reason: The current visibility function misses the sibling mesh under either explanation; mesh-discovery semantics determine whether the result is 1 or the empty-group sentinel 2.

support_relation.reason: The furniture group contains its meshes, so the supplied AABB support implementation should close the gap.

dependency_move.reason: The measured named part contract is violated by the supplied hierarchy regardless of whether that hierarchy is interpreted as intentional.

material_dependency.reason: The supplied copy-before-edit implementation and successful audit predict zero collateral changes under either explanation.

raw_evidence.source_scope: Actual SceneAct Blender compiler plus visibility/support/edit interfaces; controlled scene-description-to-Blender program repair, not natural-image end-to-end H

non_target.comparison: Exact direct comparison of matrices, local vertices, material values/nodes and parent; no hashes

raw_evidence.requirements: Compile a reusable SceneAct scene plan, retain intended world transforms and visibility, support composite furniture, preserve dependencies under group movement and local edits. Use images as desired appearance; investigate any shared module.
